title: Frontinus stratagem decoy constructor with hidden-intent outcome
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. Frontinus Strategemata I.1–4 gives complete examples where a visible action has a deceptive surface purpose and a hidden strategic intent: cutting poppy heads communicates an unspoken command, a released horse creates a false flight for reconnaissance, and a portent is reframed to induce attack. A finite constructor separates observed action, claimed intent and downstream enemy response.

source.source_span: I.1–4 preface and examples; especially Tarquin/Gabii poppy signal, horse decoy for reconnaissance, and Chabrias' portent speech
source_facts: The preface presents stratagems as tested examples intended to generate similar prudent plans.
Tarquin communicates a command through cutting the tallest poppy heads rather than stating it openly.
A horse is released and chased to create a false appearance while observers inspect a camp.
Chabrias reframes a lightning event as divine support to alter soldiers' willingness to fight.

duplicate_screen.checked: ideas search/duplicates Frontinus stratagem/decoy/hidden intent and route-check deception/sequence; Vegetius reserve card kept separate as resource-state mechanism
duplicate_screen.difference: This card is an intent/reference split in which one visible operation produces a second-party inference and response; it is not a battle-line reserve, transport sequence, or generic hidden state.

constructor.consequence: The same visible event can yield different downstream responses when observer belief or hidden intent changes; a literal-action rival predicts only cutting, horse movement, or lightning with no strategic response. A failed decoy would leave the visible action but remove the intended response.
constructor.smallest_test: Require two complete source anecdotes sharing a visible operation type but differing in observer inference and outcome, with hidden intent kept distinct from physical event.
constructor.rival: Every event means exactly its visible physical action; audience belief and strategic intent are omitted or treated as decorative narrative.
assumptions: The anecdotes are used as complete source examples of a compositional relation, not as a universal theory of deception.
Observer belief is an explicit analyst type derived from the source's stated response.
failure_modes: Frontinus is a curated catalogue of anecdotes rather than one continuous process.
The same surface action may not recur with enough source-owned structural sameness.
Without an independently bound observer and response, hidden intent is unfalsifiable.

dependencies: Source-only military examples; no target phrase or visual clue is assigned strategic meaning.
access: Source-only; no target, reserve, image, experiment, route, ledger, decoder, or root file access.
